extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PD/PIs), early career investigators, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural guidance for determining Early Stage Investigator (ESI) status for NIH R01-equivalent grant applications, and how ESI status affects peer review and funding prioritization. Includes definitions, data sources used for determination, and review/timing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an Early Stage Investigator (ESI)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESI is a Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI) who has completed their terminal research degree or end of post-graduate clinical training, whichever date is later, within the past 10 years and who has not previously competed successfully as PD/PI for a substantial NIH independent research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary eligibility standard. Note the two-part test: (1) completion date of terminal degree or end of post-graduate clinical training (whichever is later) must be within the past 10 years; and (2) the PD/PI must not have previously been successful as PD/PI on a 'substantial NIH independent research award.' See linked list of NIH grants that a PD/PI can hold and still be considered an ESI for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10-year time window for ESI eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI eligibility is based on having completed terminal research degree or end of post-graduate clinical training within the past 10 years (whichever is later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The completion date recorded in the Education section of the PI's eRA Commons profile is used to assess this time window. Extensions and exceptions may be available (see 'Early Stage Investigator Extensions' resources on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior award disqualification (no prior substantial independent NIH award)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be an ESI, the PD/PI must not have previously competed successfully as PD/PI for a substantial NIH independent research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a prior award is 'substantial' affects ESI status; NIH provides lists and guidance on which smaller grants or awards do not remove ESI status. Check the linked resources ('List of Smaller Grants & Awards that Maintain ESI Status') to determine exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy scope: applies to R01-equivalent grant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy requires NIH institutes and centers to prioritize R01-equivalent ESI applications for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prioritization and special consideration described on this page are specifically directed at R01-equivalent applications (i.e., independent research project grants considered equivalent to R01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of ESI status: funding prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI applications with scores within funding range will be prioritized for funding by the institute or center receiving the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being flagged as an ESI increases the likelihood of funding when an application falls within the institute's funding range. This is a policy-level prioritization that affects funding decisions after peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review expectations for ESI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers look more at potential than achievement—they weigh academic and research background heavily. Reviewers may expect new R01 investigators to have fewer preliminary data and publications than more established researchers do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes qualitative evaluation behavior reviewers are encouraged to adopt when assessing ESIs: greater emphasis on promise and training/background, less penalization for limited preliminary data or publication record relative to established investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and summary statement prioritization for ESIs
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI R01 applications are reviewed on the same timeline as other applications submitted to the same funding opportunity announcement. When feasible, ESI applications are not interspersed with those of established investigators at the review meeting. Summary statements for ESI R01 applications are prioritized, and when possible, released before summary statements for other applications reviewed in the same meeting. Generally, summary statements will be available no later than 30 days before Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are procedural practices intended to give ESIs distinct consideration during peer review and in the timing of summary statement release. They guide logistics of review meeting composition and timing of summary statement dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source for determining ESI eligibility (eRA Commons Education section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information from the Education section of a PI’s eRA Commons profile is used to determine ESI eligibility based on completion date of their terminal research degree or the completion date of post-graduate clinical training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure their eRA Commons Education section is accurate because the system uses that data to determine and note ESI eligibility in the PI profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of ESI determination and effect of Grants.gov submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The ESI status of the PD/PI(s) on a R01 equivalent grant application will be determined at the time of submission. If the PD/PI(s) on the application is/are classified as ESI on the date the application is successfully submitted to Grants.gov, the application will be flagged as ESI and will receive special consideration during the review and funding process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESI classification is fixed at the successful Grants.gov submission date; applicants should be aware that changes after successful submission do not change the flag. The system flags applications so institutes/centers and review staff can apply ESI prioritization policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of resources and related links
rubrics_metrics.description: The page points to related resources such as 'determining ESI status', 'Early Stage Investigator Extensions', and a 'List of Smaller Grants & Awards that Maintain ESI Status'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources provide further detail on edge cases, extension policies, and which awards do or do not affect ESI status; applicants and administrators should consult them for specific scenarios not fully described on this summary page.
